root_cause.text: drm_buddy_alloc_blocks() failed to validate the post-rounding allocation size/order against the buddy manager limits, so roundup_pow_of_two()/round_up() could inflate a request beyond mm->size and produce order > mm->max_order, triggering BUG_ON.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (order > mm->max_order || size > mm->size)` before the allocation loop and the commit message explicitly states that contiguous allocations use `roundup_pow_of_two()` and others use `round_up()`, which can make 9G become 16G on a 10G `mm`, "later trigger[ing] BUG_ON(order > mm->max_order)".

intent_record.intent_summary: Reject oversized buddy allocation requests early, while allowing contiguous non-range requests to fall back to the harder contiguous allocation path.
intent_record.what: An early conditional check was added in drm_buddy_alloc_blocks() after computing order and min_order to detect when the requested order exceeds mm->max_order or the requested size exceeds mm->size. In that case, the code now calls __alloc_contig_try_harder(mm, original_size, original_min_size, blocks) and returns its result when DRM_BUDDY_CONTIGUOUS_ALLOCATION is set and DRM_BUDDY_RANGE_ALLOCATION is not set; otherwise it returns -EINVAL.
intent_record.how: This change prevents the allocator from continuing with an invalid oversized allocation request through the normal allocation path. For oversized contiguous non-range allocations, it enables a fallback path that may still satisfy the request by trying harder, while all other oversized requests now fail immediately with -EINVAL instead of proceeding further and potentially hitting invalid state or incorrect behavior.

grouping_result.intent: Reject oversized buddy allocation requests early, while allowing contiguous non-range requests to fall back to the harder contiguous allocation path.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly adds early rejection for oversized buddy allocation requests, which addresses the root cause of failing to validate rounded allocation size/order against the buddy manager limits before reaching invalid orders/BUG_ON, while preserving the intended contiguous fallback behavior.

candidates.rationale: This statement is where the unvalidated post-rounding allocation size/order turns into a kernel BUG. Because earlier code failed to reject requests inflated beyond mm->size, order could exceed mm->max_order and trigger this BUG_ON.

This computes the allocation order from the rounded page count without validating that the resulting order still fits within the buddy manager limits. If pages was inflated past the manager size, this derived order can exceed mm->max_order.

This re-derives order from pages during allocation attempts but still lacks any bounds check against the maximum representable manager order before the BUG_ON. It directly propagates an oversized rounded request into an invalid order value.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the crashing statement reached when the allocation size was rounded up beyond the buddy manager size and the derived order exceeded mm->max_order. The missing validation of the post-rounding request turns into a security-relevant kernel BUG here.

This computes the allocation order from the rounded page count without checking that the rounded request still fits within mm->size or that the resulting order is within mm->max_order. It is part of the vulnerable path that allows an oversized request to propagate.

This statement continues to derive and use an order from the inflated page count during allocation attempts without validating it against the buddy manager limits, enabling the invalid oversized order to persist until the BUG_ON fires.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet fully shows the relevant allocation-size/order computation and validation in `drm_buddy_alloc_blocks()`, so it is sufficient to assess the root cause. The vulnerable construct is present because the function computes `pages = size >> ilog2(mm->chunk_size);` and then `order = fls(pages) - 1;`, and later repeatedly derives allocation orders from `pages` (`order = min(order, (unsigned int)fls(pages) - 1);`) without first rounding/validating the effective allocation size against `mm->size`/`mm->max_order` after any power-of-two style expansion. Instead, it only checks the original request bounds with `if (end > mm->size) return -EINVAL;` and `if (range_overflows(start, size, mm->size)) return -EINVAL;`. The function then explicitly hits `BUG_ON(order > mm->max_order);`, meaning an oversized post-rounding order can trigger the BUG described in the root cause. There is no protective check here that rejects a request whose rounded allocation size/order would exceed manager limits before reaching the `BUG_ON`. Therefore the bug is present, and the fix is not yet included.
